DNK-USA.note: NATO allies; a Sept 22, 2026 deal grants the US new Arctic bases and broad access in Greenland, easing friction over earlier US annexation talk.

IRN-ISR.note: Open war since Feb 2026 strikes that killed Ali Khamenei; June truce collapsed in July

IRN-SAU.note: Conflict deepens as Iranian-backed Houthi forces launch continuous missile and drone strikes targeting Saudi infrastructure.

IRN-USA.note: At war since Feb 2026 US-Israeli strikes; US naval blockade of Iran; talks at UNGA on a 60-day regional ceasefire

SAU-YEM.note: War escalates sharply as Houthi missiles strike the Saudi-led coalition headquarters at the presidential palace in Aden.

BEL-RWA.note: Diplomatic ties are restored after an 18-month rupture over the conflict in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC).

IRQ-TUR.note: Ankara and Baghdad agree on the handover of the Bashiqa military base to Iraqi forces amid security cooperation in Sinjar.

USA-VEN.note: Confrontation persists, but the United States (US) lifts sanctions on National Assembly head Jorge Rodríguez amid oilfield access talks.

COL-IRN.note: Colombia cuts diplomatic ties with Iran and designates the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) as a terrorist organization.

CAN-VNM.note: Canada and Vietnam establish a formal Strategic Partnership to elevate bilateral economic and security cooperation.

SAU-TUR.note: Türkiye clarifies it will not engage in combat against Houthis under the Mecca mutual defense pact with Saudi Arabia.

COL-USA.note: Long-time security partner; relations stabilize under the government of Abelardo de la Espriella.

FRA-SAU.note: France deploys military personnel to Yanbu to help protect Saudi energy infrastructure from Houthi strikes.

HUN-SVK.note: Hungary and Slovakia maintain partner ties under Prime Minister Péter Magyar and Prime Minister Robert Fico.

CHN-USA.note: Following the Trump-Xi summit, both nations agree to a $30 billion tariff cut and establish an AI safety dialogue channel.

BLZ-GTM.note: Tensions rise as Belize accuses Guatemala of violating its airspace with military aircraft and seeks international monitoring.

DEU-HUN.note: Germany and Hungary revive bilateral defense ties, agreeing to joint military exercises and Leopard tank cooperation.

HUN-UKR.note: Ties improve as Hungary lifts its veto, enabling the European Union (EU) to open new accession negotiation clusters with Ukraine.

USA-ZWE.note: Relations deteriorate as US-funded health programs in Zimbabwe end following a dispute over a data-sharing clause.

DEU-RUS.note: Germany maintains sanctions against Russia, rejecting a United States (US) agreement on Russian diesel imports.

PAK-SAU.note: Under the Mecca Joint Defense Agreement, Pakistan deploys military forces to Saudi Arabia to counter escalating Houthi attacks.

DJI-ETH.note: Strong economic partners; Djibouti and Ethiopia launch a $660 million cross-border fuel pipeline project.

ERI-ETH.note: Border tensions escalate as Eritrean troops reportedly cross into Ethiopia following severe warnings from Addis Ababa.

AFG-PAK.note: Clashes erupt along the Durand Line as Pakistani forces strike Taliban posts following cross-border infiltration attempts.

BGD-IND.note: Tensions persist as Bangladesh presses India to negotiate a renewal of the expiring Ganges Water Sharing Treaty.

MAR-SAU.note: King Mohammed VI declares any attack on Saudi Arabia is an attack on Morocco following Houthi strikes on Saudi territory.

KOR-UKR.note: South Korea recalls its ambassador to Ukraine over a diplomatic dispute regarding North Korean prisoners of war.

MDA-RUS.note: Moldova expels a Russian diplomat after a Russian drone crashes near residential homes and energy infrastructure.

JPN-USA.note: The alliance under Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi faces scrutiny over a murder linked to a United States (US) Marine in Okinawa.

ISR-NLD.note: Israel strips diplomatic credentials of Dutch envoys to Ramallah following a Dutch ban on trade in Israeli settlement products.

EGY-ETH.note: Egypt and Ethiopia expel each other's diplomats amid escalating rifts over the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam (GERD).

ETH-SDN.note: Tensions rise as Ethiopia accuses Sudan of backing anti-government armed groups in Tigray, claims Sudan denies.

ARE-ISR.note: Abraham Accords partnership strained as Israel and the UAE coordinate a response to an attack on a Flydubai flight.

ISR-MAR.note: Israel and Morocco upgrade reciprocal missions to full embassies, formalizing their Abraham Accords partnership.

POL-RUS.note: Poland readies air defences and scrambles fighters after a Russian drone strikes Ukraine two kilometres from the Polish border.

PRK-RUS.note: North Korea prepares to deploy 10,000 additional troops to support Russian operations in Ukraine.

ARG-GBR.note: Argentine President Milei rules out military force over the Falkland Islands, committing to pursue diplomatic channels.

MMR-MYS.note: Malaysia repatriates over 10,000 Myanmar nationals since January, even as Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim prepares to host junta chief.

KHM-VNM.note: Vietnam and Cambodia deepen defence cooperation and border security coordination under high-level bilateral agreements.

CHE-RUS.note: Switzerland rejects a constitutional initiative to tighten neutrality, maintaining its ability to join sanctions against Russia.

EST-RUS.note: Estonia accuses Russian special services of ordering an arson attack on a local defense-robotics manufacturer.

KOR-PRK.note: North Korea prepares border loudspeaker broadcasts and mobilizes forces following DMZ (Demilitarized Zone) mine explosions.

ESP-ISR.note: Israel reprimands the Spanish envoy after a Spanish minister made controversial 'river to sea' remarks.

CAN-USA.note: NATO, NORAD and USMCA partners; tensions persist over tariffs under Prime Minister Mark Carney.

IRQ-USA.note: United States forces complete their military withdrawal from Iraq, ending the anti-ISIS combat mission.

KEN-RWA.note: Kenya delivers its first 40,000-tonne fuel shipment to Rwanda via Mombasa under a new bilateral energy supply route.

CHN-LAO.note: China opens a joint aviation training and support center in Laos, marking its third overseas military facility.

CUB-USA.note: Relations strain further as Florida authorities issue an arrest warrant and bring new charges against Raúl Castro.

BDI-USA.note: Burundi agrees to accept US-deported migrants under a third-country resettlement policy.

COL-ECU.note: Colombia extradites the family of Ecuadorian gang leader 'Fito' to Ecuador, boosting security cooperation.

BRA-USA.note: Strained by tariffs and sanctions, though both nations maintain trade ties under President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva.

GBR-USA.note: Close NATO and Five Eyes allies coordinate as the US withdraws B-1 bombers from RAF Fairford over Iranian-backed security threats.

KOR-USA.note: Allies clash after USFK (US Forces Korea) commander remarks prompt South Korean officials to defend DMZ (Demilitarized Zone) sovereignty.

GBR-ISR.note: Israel downgrades the United Kingdom's consulate in Jerusalem to a mission over sanctions targeting West Bank settlements.

EGY-USA.note: The United States (US) waives human rights restrictions on $320 million in military aid to Egypt, citing regional security concerns.

DEU-UKR.note: Germany supports Ukraine under Chancellor Friedrich Merz, pledging military aid and drone cooperation.

FRA-TUR.note: France and Türkiye sign a defense roadmap in Ankara to expand military and security cooperation.

DZA-NER.note: Algeria's parliament and president approve deploying army units to protect energy assets and shared interests in Niger.

ARM-TUR.note: Armenia and Türkiye agree on student exchanges as negotiations to reopen their shared border continue.

CHN-PRK.note: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un visits China via the newly opened Dandong bridge for high-level talks.

ISR-LBN.note: Tensions escalate as Israel warns Lebanon over Hezbollah-linked weapons and cross-border security threats.

RUS-SYR.note: Ties fray as Russia refuses to extradite ousted leader Bashar al-Assad to Syria following a death sentence handed down in Damascus.

KHM-TUR.note: Cambodia and Türkiye sign a defence cooperation deal to strengthen bilateral military and security ties.

BLR-PRK.note: Belarus opens a resident embassy in North Korea to expand bilateral diplomatic and economic ties.

CRI-SLV.note: Costa Rica and El Salvador sign a new bilateral agreement to combat transnational organized crime.

ROU-RUS.note: Tensions heighten after a Russian drone strike sinks a merchant ship near Romanian waters, killing a crew member.

CHN-JPN.note: Tensions persist as China condemns Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi for sending a ritual offering to the Yasukuni Shrine.

BLR-UKR.note: Hostile relations persist as Ukraine warns Belarus may host Russian ballistic missiles for strikes targeting its western regions.

ETH-SOL.note: Somaliland reaffirms support for Ethiopia's sea access quest and discusses bilateral defense cooperation amid regional tensions.

BEL-COD.note: The DR Congo (DRC) freezes contacts with Belgium after Belgian authorities raid the residences of presidential associates.

NGA-RWA.note: Nigeria and Rwanda deepen defence ties, agreeing to joint military equipment production and cadet exchange programs.

USA-UZB.note: The US and Uzbekistan expand economic and security ties, signing over $12 billion in contracts during diplomatic talks.

SDN-SSD.note: Sudan and South Sudan face escalating tensions after a deadly Sudanese drone strike hits an Abyei market.

DNK-VNM.note: Denmark and Vietnam elevate bilateral ties to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership to expand green energy and tech cooperation.

GBR-SAU.note: Britain expands its military support for Saudi Arabia to defend key infrastructure against escalating Houthi strikes.

MDV-PAK.note: Pakistan and the Maldives sign 20 Memorandums of Understanding (MoU) to expand cooperation in defense and maritime security.

GRC-TUR.note: Tensions persist as Greece rejects eastern Libya's ratification of a contested maritime boundary agreement with Turkey.

GUY-USA.note: The United States (US) and Guyana elevate security ties under a new Enhanced Defense Agreement to strengthen sovereignty.

ARG-ESP.note: Tensions flare after Argentine President Milei calls Spanish Prime Minister Sánchez a dictator during a visit to Madrid.

AUS-TLS.note: Australia and Timor-Leste sign a new security agreement to enhance maritime and cyber defense.

SAU-USA.note: The US orders non-essential diplomats to leave Saudi Arabia as Houthi drone and missile strikes target Saudi infrastructure.

HTI-SLV.note: El Salvador expands its security deployment in Haiti to over 2,000 troops to assist in combating armed gangs.

RUS-UKR.note: Russia and Ukraine agree to a ceasefire in Oleshky, brokered by Melania Trump, amid a severe food crisis.

CAN-TUR.note: Canada and Türkiye launch a Strategic Partnership to expand trade, defense, and energy cooperation.

ESP-ITA.note: Spain and Italy end border restrictions and resolve the diplomatic crisis triggered by the Ceuta migration influx.

IND-POL.note: India and Poland agree to expand strategic ties in defence, space, and nuclear energy.

AUT-RUS.note: Austria expels four Russian diplomats for espionage, prompting a vow of retaliation from Moscow.

ETH-KEN.note: Fighting in the border town of Moyale kills nine and forces thousands of Ethiopians to flee into Kenya.

IDN-SGP.note: Tensions rise after Indonesia cuts natural gas exports to Singapore following bilateral friction.

RUS-UGA.note: Uganda and Russia expand military ties as Moscow delivers a $53 million defense support package and opens joint facilities.

DZA-FRA.note: Tensions persist as Algeria moves to halt urea exports to France amid an ongoing diplomatic rift.

POL-VNM.note: Poland and Vietnam establish a Strategic Partnership to strengthen bilateral trade, defense, and economic cooperation.

JOR-SYR.note: Jordan and Syria reopen the Nasib border crossing and establish a joint security committee following recent airstrikes.

MDA-UKR.note: Moldova and Ukraine sign a five-year defense cooperation agreement to strengthen security against Russian threats.

ETH-RUS.note: Ethiopia strengthens defence ties with Russia after acquiring 12 Su-35 fighter jets and agreeing to buy S-400 air defence systems.

houthi-red-sea.d: Iran-backed Houthi forces target Saudi oil refineries and infrastructure, triggering global oil price surges and regional defense responses.

afpak-jihad.d: Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) and Islamic State Khorasan Province (ISKP) operate from Afghan sanctuaries, triggering cross-border Pakistani counter-strikes and fatal military clashes along the Durand Line.

indus.d: Water allocation in the Indus basin remains contentious as Pakistan warns India that diverting river flows would constitute an act of war.

sudan-war.n: Sudan's war and its outside backers
sudan-war.d: Sudan's civil war intensifies with drone strikes in Abyei and Chad, as regional powers vie for influence.

cocaine-europe.n: Cocaine via West Africa & the Sahel to Europe
cocaine-europe.d: Andean cocaine transits West Africa, including Sierra Leone and Guinea-Bissau, toward European markets, triggering diplomatic sanctions.

cocaine-americas.d: Andean cocaine moves through Central America and Mexico to the United States (US); the US deploys MQ-9 Reaper drones to Colombia and Ecuador to monitor trafficking routes.

africa-corps.d: Russia's Africa Corps backs Sahel juntas; Malian forces successfully reclaim the rebel stronghold of Kidal with Russian military support.

captagon.d: Captagon produced in Syria and Lebanon moves through Jordan, Iraq, and maritime routes to consumers in the Gulf and North Africa, prompting joint interdictions.

kurdish.d: Kurdish groups face shifting fronts as the PKK (Kurdistan Workers' Party) vacates northern Iraq camps in a Turkish peace bid, while Iranian drones strike KDPI (Democratic Party of Iranian Kurdistan) bases in Koya.

sahel-gold.d: Artisanal gold from the Sahel and the Egypt-Sudan border is smuggled to the United Arab Emirates (UAE) and Switzerland, funding armed factions.

golden-triangle.d: Syndicates operate scam centers and drug labs across Myanmar borderlands targeting global victims, prompting Chinese-led cross-border trials.

central-med.d: Migrants from Africa and Asia transit eastern Libya and Tunisia toward Italy and Greece as the European Union (EU) funds regional interdiction.

baloch.d: BLA (Balochistan Liberation Army) insurgents strike Pakistani military convoys and CPEC (China-Pakistan Economic Corridor) assets in Gwadar, provoking security crackdowns.

bab-el-mandeb.d: The strategic strait remains highly volatile as Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces claim control of the area following a major offensive against Houthis.

pituffik-space-base.d: Missile-warning radar in Greenland. A Sept 22, 2026 US-Denmark agreement added two further US sites, at Narsarsuaq and Mestersvig, with broad air and undersea access, easing friction from Trump's earlier annexation talk.
pituffik-space-base.s: Northernmost US base; 2 more Greenland sites added Sept 2026

strait-of-hormuz.d: Iran threatens subsea cables while tanker attacks near the strait cause major oil spills off the United Arab Emirates (UAE).

suwa-ki-gap.s: NATO weak spot · Poland and Lithuania draft evacuation plan Sept 2026

wakhan-corridor.d: Afghanistan opens a 121-kilometer road through the corridor to the Chinese border, aiming to establish direct trade.

strait-of-magellan.d: Diplomatic friction rises as the United States (US) presses Chile to align passage rights through the strategic waterway with Washington.

eastern-dr-congo.s: M23 rebrands as FRN under Kabila
eastern-dr-congo.d: The M23-led AFC (Alliance Fleuve Congo) rebrands as the FRN with former DR Congo president Joseph Kabila heading Doha peace talks.

falkland-islands.d: Argentina challenges Falklands oil drilling at an international tribunal as the United Kingdom (UK) stages military defence drills.

abyei.d: Contested border region between Sudan and South Sudan; a Sudanese army drone strike on an Abyei market killed over 150 people.

korean-dmz.d: Tensions rise as North Korea fortifies the Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) with approximately one million landmines since 2024.

syunik-tripp-route.d: Transit corridor connecting Azerbaijan to Nakhchivan; Armenia's parliament ratified the TRIPP (Transit Route) framework agreement.
